title: Pair-balanced rational controls and affine tempered binary orbits

concepts.label: pair-balanced coefficient control
concepts.note: A bounded binary payload is moved between positions 2k and 2k+1 while preserving the total dyadic value of each pair.

concepts.label: explicit tempered carry orbit
concepts.note: The coefficient control carries an explicit multiplier-nine integer orbit whose even coordinates retain the payload.

concepts.label: affine rank-two control
concepts.note: Identity coefficients admit the multiplier-one orbit u(N)=N+2, separating temperedness from finite-rank or irrationality conclusions.

concepts.label: rational-control boundary
concepts.note: These are rational control families in the generic linear-growth class; they are not Euler's totient coefficients or arbitrary infinite-support coefficients and prove neither Erdős 249 nor 257.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For the pair-balanced control, the coefficients are k-a(k) at index 2k and 2a(k) at index 2k+1. Its explicit multiplier-nine orbit is 3k+4+9a(k) at index 2k and 6k+8 at index 2k+1.
statement_nodes.engine: Parity splitting and exact simplification of the two defining if-then-else expressions.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Exact evaluations of an explicit control family; no novelty claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The coordinate formulas concern an artificial rational control family, not the totient sequence, and do not imply an irrationality or nonintegrality statement.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If a(0)=0 and every payload digit a(k) is at most one, then the pair-balanced coefficient sequence satisfies c(n)≤n, its explicit multiplier-nine orbit is tempered, and the resulting binary coefficient series is exactly 4/9 for every such payload.
statement_nodes.engine: The parity formulas give linear growth and the exact carry recurrence; an affine-over-geometric estimate proves temperedness, after which tail-orbit rigidity evaluates the series.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: An explicit rational control model used to test the strength of generic tail-orbit arguments.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The theorem demonstrates that rich bounded payloads can coexist with a fixed rational value. It does not construct a totient-series model, refute a valid totient-specific invariant, or decide Erdős 249.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: At every even coordinate 2k, subtracting the zero-payload orbit from the orbit with payload a gives exactly 9a(k). Thus the arbitrary bounded payload remains explicitly visible in the carry even though every control has the same series value 4/9.
statement_nodes.engine: Direct subtraction of the two exact even-coordinate orbit formulas.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: An exact payload-decoding identity for the explicit control family.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Payload recovery is a no-go witness for overly coarse generic state summaries only; it is not an obstruction theorem for the actual totient sequence.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The identity coefficient sequence c(n)=n has the explicit multiplier-one tempered orbit u(N)=N+2. Hence a coefficient family may have an affine, rank-two section structure while still satisfying the exact tempered carry recurrence.
statement_nodes.engine: A direct recurrence calculation followed by the classical limit N/2^N→0.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The identity coefficients are not Euler's totient function. This control prevents finite-rank structure alone from being read as an irrationality criterion.

intra_zone_relations.basis: The parity formulas supply the recurrence and growth calculations used by the tempered-orbit and fixed-value theorem.
It shows that the fixed rational value does not erase the arbitrary payload from the carry state.
